fact: Firestone's development code says artificial turf shall not be installed over existing grass or compacted dirt.
quote: Artificial turf shall not be installed over existing grass or compacted dirt.
source_label: Firestone Development Code 16.6.4.F.2.e.iii (codified through Ord. No. 1072, Dec. 10, 2025)
notes: Read 2026-09-25 through the Municode API (api.municode.com/CodesContent, productId 18062, jobId 488870, node TIT16FIDECO_CH6DEDEST_16.6.4LASCFE). The sentence follows the 3-inch aggregate-base sentence in F.2.e.iii; that clause and the rest of the standard stay with firestone-fdc-16.6.4-turf-specs and the turf-spec-sheet-for-colorado guide (editor note: cite only the clause this page needs). F.2.e.ii in the same list: 'The drainage pattern of the lot shall not be impeded or altered by the installation of artificial turf.'

fact: Firestone's development code applies its landscaping section, 16.6.4, to single-family lots and houses that existed before the code was adopted, not only to new development.
quote: Individual single-family residential lots and structures existing before the adoption of this FDC shall be subject to the following Sections of this Chapter: Sections 16.6.4 ; 16.6.6 ; 16.6.11 ; and 16.6.12 .
source_label: Firestone Development Code 16.6.1.B, Applicability (codified through Ord. No. 1072, Dec. 10, 2025)
notes: Read 2026-09-25 through the Municode API (same job as the 16.6.4 record). Spacing before the semicolons is as the code prints it.

fact: CSU Extension's PlantTalk Colorado says field bindweed roots grow 20 feet or more deep and sideways, that a root can grow into new plants, and that its seeds can survive for 20 years.
quote: Field bindweed is a noxious perennial weed that is difficult to kill because of its extensive root system. Roots grow deeply, 20 feet or more, as well as laterally. The root is capable of growing into new plants. … prevent the vine from producing seeds as they can survive for 20 years … Bindweed is a sun-loving plant, so shading it out with cloth or other plants can be an effective control.
source_label: CSU Extension, PlantTalk Colorado 2104, Controlling Bindweed

fact: CSU Extension's lawn-removal guide says a sod cutter takes a lawn out quickly in rolled strips that can be given away, but it needs heavy equipment and leaves the question of how to get rid of the sod, which can instead be flipped over to decompose in place under compost and mulch.
quote: Use a sod cutter – If your lawn is in good condition, you can cut strips with a sod cutter, roll them up and give them away. First, mow and water your lawn. Cut overlapping strips of sod and roll them up. Cut strips short enough to be moved easily. This method is quick but requires heavy equipment and you are left with the dilemma of how to get rid of the rolls of sod. Alternatively, you can flip the sod over to decompose in place, keeping the organic matter in your yard or garden. You then treat it like the ‘mow and cover’ method. Cover with compost and mulch and water to promote decomposition.
source_label: CSU Extension, PlantTalk Colorado: How to Remove All (or Part) of Your Lawn (PDF)
notes: Written for turning lawn into planting beds, not for turf; the page uses it for the sod cutter and for where sod can go, and says plainly that decomposing sod in place belongs in a planted bed, never under turf.

fact: CSU Extension says killing a lawn with herbicide leaves the dead grass and roots in place to decompose, and that smothering a scalped lawn under compost and 8–12 inches of wood chips can take a season or more and still may not kill all of the bluegrass.
quote: It maintains the soil’s structure and microbiology and leaves the organic content (dead grass and roots) in place to decompose. … Mow close and cover – Withhold water from the area to stress the grass. Scalp it by mowing it as close as possible. Then cover the area with compost and an 8-12” layer of woodchips. … Be aware that this will take a season or more and still may not kill all of the bluegrass.
source_label: CSU Extension, PlantTalk Colorado: How to Remove All (or Part) of Your Lawn (PDF)
notes: The first sentence describes spraying with a non-selective herbicide. The same guide's solarizing method covers the lawn with clear plastic for 4-8 weeks, most effective June through August.

fact: CSU Extension says digging a lawn out brings weed seeds to the surface where they germinate, and tilling a lawn under can spread bindweed and Canada thistle.
quote: Dig it up – Water the area thoroughly to soften the soil. Dig up the grass, thatch and roots. … It also disturbs the soil’s structure and brings weed seeds to the surface where the warmth and moisture germinate them. … This method does destroy soil structure and can propagate weeds like bindweed and Canada thistle.
source_label: CSU Extension, PlantTalk Colorado: How to Remove All (or Part) of Your Lawn (PDF)
notes: The last sentence is from the guide's 'Till it under' method.

fact: The Synthetic Turf Council's base-system guidelines say organic soils are unstable, sensitive to water and low in load-bearing capacity, and that building a turf base starts by digging out the organic soil.
quote: Organic soils are to be avoided in a synthetic field sub-base. These soils are unstable, are sensitive to water and have a low load-bearing capacity. … Organic soils are not appropriate for sub-grade preparation. The first operation in the base construction process is to excavate and eliminate the organic soil that covers the work area.
source_label: Synthetic Turf Council, Guidelines for Synthetic Turf Base Systems (February 2017), sections 4.2.2.4 and 5.1.1.2
notes: Written for sports fields; the page says so and applies it to a yard by analogy. The document allows brief quotation in review; keep quotes short.

fact: The Synthetic Turf Council's base-system guidelines say freeze-thaw cycles in cold climates push rocks toward the surface, and that big rocks and boulders under a turf base can threaten it over time.
quote: Freeze-thaw cycles typically cause rocks to migrate towards the surface. This is a natural phenomenon that cannot be stopped. Small rocks do not pose a problem because the stone base that is laid over the surface will stop their upward progression. But big rocks and boulders can present a threat to the base’s integrity over time.
source_label: Synthetic Turf Council, Guidelines for Synthetic Turf Base Systems (February 2017), section 4.2.2.5
notes: Written for sports fields in cold climates; the page applies it to a cobble or river-rock bed by analogy.

fact: FieldTurf's landscape installation guide says to remove grass, sod, roots, mulch and rocks with a sod cutter, shovel and pickaxe, and that artificial grass should not simply be placed over untreated soil.
quote: Use a sod cutter, shovel, and pickaxe to remove grass, sod, roots, mulch, and rocks. Grade the sub-base. … Artificial grass should not simply be placed over untreated soil. Proper excavation, grading, base preparation, drainage planning, and compaction help create a stable foundation.
source_label: FieldTurf Landscape, How to Install Artificial Grass: Complete Installation Guide
notes: A manufacturer's published instructions (FieldTurf is a Tarkett brand). The page quotes the removal step only; the base depth on the same page belongs to what-base-goes-under-artificial-turf.

fact: The Federal Highway Administration's gravel-roads guide says crushed stone interlocks with the particles around it, while rounded natural stone shifts and moves under loads more easily.
quote: Gravel has more strength when there are more crushed particles since they will interlock better with the particles surrounding them. Natural stone with a rounded shape will tend to shift and move under loads more easily.
source_label: Federal Highway Administration and South Dakota LTAP, Gravel Roads Construction & Maintenance Guide (August 2015)
notes: Written for road gravel; the page applies it to pea gravel under turf by analogy (pea gravel is rounded natural stone).

fact: Larimer County's Green Waste Program takes grass, leaves, brush and branches but not root balls or soil, and sends mixed loads to the landfill.
quote: We will not accept the following as green waste: Bags, containers, fiberboard, food waste, metal, painted wood, plastic, plywood, root balls, soil, trash, treated wood, trunks larger than 2 feet in diameter (these cannot be processed as green waste) and weeds. … All green waste loads must be clean and unloaded by waste type (pallets, green waste, logs, and yard waste). No other trash will be accepted in a load; all mixed loads will go to the landfill.
source_label: Larimer County Solid Waste, Green Waste Program
notes: larimer.gov serves a Cloudflare challenge to curl and headless browsers. Live page read 2026-09-25 through WebFetch (the exclusion sentence matched word for word); the verbatim text was confirmed against the Wayback capture https://web.archive.org/web/20260216043333/https://www.larimer.gov/solidwaste/greenwaste. Re-read in a browser by the recheck date.

fact: Larimer County's 2026 landfill fee schedule lists sod and dirt as rubble at $40 per cubic yard plus the state surcharge, prices clean dirt by the load, and applies to both landfills and the transfer station.
quote: Rubble (concrete, dirt, sod, asphalt, tree trunks, sludge, non-friable asbestos, and other materials) >1,000 lbs per cubic yard … $40 per cubic yard + CO surcharge … Clean dirt (tandem) … $100 per load … The Transfer Station and North Landfill opened on August 3, 2026. The pricing listed is for both Landfills and the Transfer Station.
source_label: Larimer County Solid Waste, 2026 Landfill Fee Schedule
notes: Cloudflare blocks curl; read 2026-09-25 through WebFetch, twice, asking for the rows character for character (both reads matched). The schedule does not say which site accepts rubble; the page says 'check which county site takes it'. Fees change yearly: re-read in a browser by the recheck date.

fact: Larimer County closed its landfill on August 3, 2026, moved waste disposal to the Central Diversion & Transfer Station on West Trilby Road, and opened a North Landfill near Wellington for commercial haulers and nearby residents.
quote: Effective August 3, 2026, the Larimer County Landfill will be CLOSED, and all waste disposal services will be moved to the Central Diversion & Transfer Station (2388 West Trilby Road). … The Larimer County North Landfill (15669 North County Road 9, Wellington, CO 80549) will open on August 3rd, 2026, for commercial haulers, and residents who live in and near Wellington (about a 10-mile radius for the North Landfill) including the communities of Livermore, Red Feather Lakes, Carr, and Waverly.
notes: Cloudflare blocks curl; read 2026-09-25 through WebFetch, twice, with the same wording both times. Estes Valley Voice (2026-08-08, https://estesvalleyvoice.com/2026/08/08/larimer-county-opens-new-transfer-station-landfill/) reports both sites opened on Aug. 3, 2026. The old entrance at 5887 S. Taft Hill Road stays open only for recycling haulers, household hazardous waste, electronics recycling, the education center and the business office.

source_label: City of Loveland, Recycling Center (400 N. Wilson Ave.)
notes: lovgov.org returns 403 to curl and to WebFetch. Read verbatim in the Wayback capture https://web.archive.org/web/20260501195810/https://www.lovgov.org/services/public-works/trash-recycling/recycling-center (the capture lists 2026 holiday closures, so it is the 2026 page). fact: The City of Fort Collins's Recycling A to Z guide says sod can be composted in a backyard pile or at the drop-off locations it lists, where fees may apply.
quote: Sod can be composted in your backyard compost pile or at the drop-off locations listed below. Fees may apply. Contact location for details.
source_label: City of Fort Collins, Recycling A to Z Guide: Sod
notes: The locations listed on 2026-09-25 are three private businesses, two in Fort Collins and one in Eaton; the page does not name them.

fact: The City of Fort Collins's Recycling A to Z guide says clean fill dirt can be taken for reuse at the locations it lists, including the City's Crushing Operations Facility.
quote: Fill dirt can be accepted for reuse at the locations listed below. Loads of dirt should be clean and uncontaminated with other material. Contact specific location for details. … City of Fort Collins Crushing Operations Facility
source_label: City of Fort Collins, Recycling A to Z Guide: Fill Dirt
notes: The other two locations listed on 2026-09-25 are private businesses.

fact: Greeley's GROW Center, open to Greeley and Weld County residents, takes green waste and topsoil but not fill dirt or rocks, at $10.00 per cubic yard, cash only.
quote: The facility is available for use by Greeley and Weld County residents, including those in neighboring communities. … All Material - $10.00/CY … Topsoil (NO FILL DIRT) … Green waste … No rocks, concrete or metal including t-posts. … CASH ONLY!
source_label: City of Greeley, Greeley Organic Waste (GROW) Center flyer (linked from greeleyco.gov Recycling)
notes: The flyer is undated; it is the one linked from https://greeleyco.gov/residents/resources/recycling/ on 2026-09-25. It does not list sod by name, so the page says to call before hauling sod there. The site is run by DBB Land and Compost, LLC under contract with the City, at a new location on North 25th Avenue.

fact: Colorado 811 says anyone digging, whatever the project's size, is legally required to contact Colorado 811 at least three business days before digging, and to dig by hand within 18 inches of a public utility mark.
quote: Regardless of your project’s size, you are legally required to contact Colorado 811 at least three business days before you dig. … Always dig cautiously with hand tools when digging within 18 inches of a mark or flag for a public utility line.
notes: Colorado 811 marks public utility lines only, so private lines such as sprinkler pipe are the owner's to find.
